sections.commitments:
LeakDetectAI commits to releasing all grant-funded, non-sensitive software, detection tooling, benchmark suites, test cases, documentation, and integration examples under an OSI-approved open-source license, preferably Apache-2.0, with source code and development history publicly available in the project's GitHub repositories. Any existing components with different licenses will retain their original licenses, and their licensing compatibility will be reviewed before integration. No grant-funded core functionality will be made exclusively available through a proprietary service.

We commit to maintaining the open-source repositories after the grant period, including preserving documentation, addressing critical bugs, reviewing community contributions, and keeping the detection and regression-testing infrastructure usable. We will make reasonable efforts to coordinate ongoing maintenance with the relevant Ethereum wallet, agent-framework, and open-source maintainers. The project will also document installation, testing, and integration procedures so that other developers can independently use and extend the work without depending on the original team.

For ecosystem adoption, we commit to pursuing the named targets MetaMask, Rabby, Trust Wallet, Safe, Coinbase AgentKit, and ElizaOS. The adoption objective is verified remediation in at least three named projects, including at least one Ethereum wallet and one agent framework. Evidence will consist of publicly verifiable issues, maintainer-reviewed fixes, merged pull requests or downstream commits, and regression tests, subject to responsible-disclosure requirements. These projects are pinned adoption targets for engagement and evaluation, not claimed partnerships or guaranteed commitments from their maintainers. Where a target has no reproducible vulnerability within the project's scope, or its maintainers decline participation, we will document the outcome and pursue another relevant Ethereum wallet or agent framework with equivalent adoption potential.

We are not requesting an exception to the open-source licensing or public-goods commitments. The only qualification is that existing third-party components retain their original licenses and security-sensitive vulnerability details may remain confidential until responsible disclosure permits publication. We will not use confidentiality as a reason to withhold non-sensitive grant-funded deliverables or the evidence needed to verify completed security improvements.
sections.in_scope:
LeakDetectAI will deliver the adoption of an open-source security testing and remediation capability across Ethereum wallets, hardware wallets, AI-agent frameworks, and Layer 2 ecosystems. The funding will support the integration of LeakDetectAI into the actual security-testing and development workflows of participating projects, collaboration with their maintainers to identify and reproduce exploitable side-channel weaknesses, and engineering support to implement and verify fixes. The central deliverable is not simply a tool that detects potential information leakage, but demonstrable security improvements in Ethereum projects that use it.

Adoption will be pursued across six areas. First, LeakDetectAI will be adopted for desktop, mobile, and hardware-wallet security testing, covering real-world key-management, transaction-signing, and authorization workflows. The work will engage relevant wallet developers and hardware-wallet testing environments to identify reproducible weaknesses, provide actionable remediation guidance, and support fixes and regression tests. Second, the existing Ethereum field deployments, including the Ethereum Layer 1 and 2 based hardware-wallet testing workflow using Ledger, will be used to apply LeakDetectAI in practical environments. The objective is to translate findings from these deployments into documented, actionable security improvements in the participating applications and their associated workflows.

Third, adoption will extend across Ethereum agent and protocol ecosystems, including relevant teams and applications within Optimism and Arbitrum. LeakDetectAI will be applied to agent execution, transaction authorization, signing, and protocol-integrated workflows, with participating developers supported in reproducing and remediating confirmed weaknesses. Fourth, we will work with Ethereum wallet developers, with prospective targets including MetaMask, Rabby Wallet, and Safe, to identify side-channel vulnerabilities affecting wallet security and support maintainers in implementing fixes. Fifth, we will engage Ethereum agent-framework developers, with prospective targets including Coinbase AgentKit and ElizaOS, to identify weaknesses in agent execution and transaction workflows and support code-level remediation and regression testing. These are prospective adoption targets, not confirmed commitments; engagement and remediation will be pursued in coordination with the relevant maintainers.

The sixth area will consolidate these efforts into ecosystem-wide adoption and verified security remediation. We target adoption by at least three named Ethereum wallet or agent-framework projects and at least three implemented security improvements in participating codebases, including wallet and agent-framework environments. Each counted improvement must be linked to a reproducible weakness identified through LeakDetectAI and supported by verifiable evidence of remediation, such as a merged patch, released fix, downstream code change, or equivalent maintainer-confirmed implementation, together with a regression test or repeatable validation showing that the weakness has been addressed. Deliverables will include documented integrations, vulnerability reproduction reports, remediation records, regression tests, and a public adoption report, subject to responsible-disclosure requirements.

The $60,000 requested will fund the adoption work required to achieve these outcomes: deployment and testing across desktop, mobile, and hardware-wallet environments; integration into existing Ethereum field deployments; engagement with Ethereum and Layer 2 agent and protocol teams; direct collaboration with wallet and agent-framework maintainers; vulnerability reproduction and remediation support; implementation of security fixes and regression tests; and independent verification and documentation of the resulting improvements. Of the total request, $50,000 (Milestones B to D) pays only on outside teams using LeakDetectAI and merging its fixes. This allocation will support the engineering effort and maintainer coordination needed to move identified vulnerabilities through to implemented fixes.

The success of the initiative will be measured by security improvements in real Ethereum projects, rather than downloads, user counts, demonstrations, or the number of testing runs. By completion, participating projects will have used LeakDetectAI to identify actionable side-channel weaknesses and address them through implemented fixes and regression tests. This will make Ethereum safer by reducing opportunities for attackers to exploit observable execution behaviour to infer sensitive information, strengthening the protection of wallet keys and signing operations, improving transaction authorization security, and reducing the exposure of AI-agent workflows to side-channel attacks. All non-sensitive tooling, remediation guidance, and verification evidence will be published as reusable open-source resources so that other Ethereum developers can adopt the same protections.
sections.out_scope:
LeakDetectAI will not undertake general-purpose privacy research, academic research without a direct Ethereum security application, or the development of new foundational machine-learning or side-channel analysis algorithms unrelated to the project's defined objectives. The initiative is not intended to build a general-purpose privacy auditing platform, surveillance or user-monitoring system, or a commercial security product. It will not cover non-Ethereum ecosystems, or other unrelated blockchain networks; the scope is strictly limited to Ethereum, its Layer 2 ecosystems, and the wallets and agent frameworks serving them.

The grant will not fund the development of new wallets, blockchain protocols, consensus clients, agent frameworks, or general-purpose AI infrastructure. It will not include broad penetration-testing engagements, smart-contract auditing unrelated to the identified side-channel risks, formal verification of entire applications, or remediation of vulnerabilities outside the project's defined threat model. It will also not fund speculative vulnerability research that cannot be connected to a concrete Ethereum security risk or actionable remediation.

Finally, the project will not publicly disclose exploitable vulnerabilities before maintainers have had a reasonable opportunity to address them. Sensitive findings, exploit details, and affected code will be handled through responsible-disclosure processes. Funding is specifically for the development and application of Ethereum-focused detection capabilities, vulnerability validation, maintainer-supported remediation, and independently verifiable improvements to Ethereum wallet and agent security; activities outside these boundaries are excluded.
sections.team:
LeakDetectAI is led by Manu Gupta, Project Lead, and Dr. Pritha Gupta, Research Lead. Together, they bring complementary experience in open-source infrastructure, decentralized systems, AI, cryptography, side-channel analysis, and automated security testing.

Manu Gupta: Project Lead | Open-Source Security and P2P Maintainer
Manu brings over 20 years of open-source engineering experience, with a track record spanning decentralized networking, cryptographic infrastructure, distributed systems, and security engineering. He is a Technical Lead and Maintainer in the libp2p ecosystem and has contributed to IPFS, IPLD, and Multiformats, including work across Go, Rust, JavaScript, and Python implementations, interoperability, protocol specifications, and network security. For LeakDetectAI, he leads project delivery, Ethereum and wallet ecosystem integration, open-source development, adoption by external projects, and coordination with maintainers to turn identified vulnerabilities into verified fixes.
Profile: https://github.com/seetadev

Dr. Pritha Gupta: Adoption and Research Lead | AI, Cryptography and Side-Channel Security
Dr. Pritha Gupta brings research experience in AI, cryptography, side-channel analysis, and automated security testing, including work associated with Ruhr-Universität Bochum and Software Innovation Campus Paderborn. She leads the technical methodology underpinning LeakDetectAI, including adversarial inference experiments, machine-learning and neural architecture search (NAS) pipelines, detection methodology, and security benchmarks. She also supports the translation of research capabilities into reproducible testing workflows and practical adoption by wallet and agent developers.
Research profile: https://sec4ai-ai4sec.github.io/

Existing funding and technical foundation
LeakDetectAI has previously received community support through the Giveth / Ethereum Security Quadratic Funding round, including community contributions and matching-pool support. This provides an initial community-backed funding foundation. The present request is for dedicated funding to support Ethereum ecosystem adoption, integrations, remediation engineering, and verification of security improvements. No additional grant amount or funding commitment is being represented here beyond that community support.

The initiative builds on existing side-channel analysis and automated security-testing work, including AutoSCA, developed in the context of Achelos. AutoSCA demonstrates the practical application of automated analysis and machine learning to identify cryptographic side-channel vulnerabilities, including Bleichenbacher-style TLS vulnerabilities. The underlying research direction is documented in the ACM AISec paper, Automated Detection of Side Channels in Cryptographic Protocols: DROWN the ROBOTs! LeakDetectAI extends this technical direction to Ethereum wallets, transaction signing, hardware-wallet workflows, and AI-agent applications.

sections.why:
Ethereum wallets, protocols, and autonomous AI agents handle sensitive information, including private keys, signing secrets, cryptographic operations, and transaction data. Yet timing variations and other side-channel signals can expose this information even when software behaves as designed. Conventional security testing often overlooks these vulnerabilities because it focuses on functional correctness rather than unintended information leakage.

LeakDetectAI closes this gap by bringing AI-powered side-channel detection into real-world Ethereum security workflows. It enables developers and security teams to identify and reproduce hidden vulnerabilities, validate fixes, and introduce regression tests that prevent them from returning. This makes it possible to detect and remediate security weaknesses that conventional testing may miss, strengthening the protection of Ethereum wallets, protocols, and AI agents.
sections.why_grant:
LeakDetectAI has an existing open-source foundation in automated side-channel analysis, machine-learning-based leakage detection, and hardware-wallet security testing. This is not a proposal to build side-channel analysis from scratch: the team has already published and made available the underlying research code and experimentation infrastructure. Public work includes:

Hardware-wallet testing and Ethereum/Web3 security: https://github.com/SEC4AI-AI4SEC/autosca-hw-wallet-tester 
The active development repository for automated side-channel security testing, including hardware-wallet analysis.

Deep-learning side-channel analysis: https://github.com/SEC4AI-AI4SEC/deep-learning-sca
An existing research and reproducibility codebase for automated side-channel analysis.

Quantitative information-leakage detection: https://github.com/SEC4AI-AI4SEC/AutoMLQuantILDetect 
An existing package applying AutoML and information-theoretic methods to detect and quantify leakage.

Project resources and demonstrations: LeakDetectAI project github site, project dashboard and and public research discussions: 
https://github.com/SEC4AI-AI4SEC/deep-learning-sca/discussions/3 and https://x.com/libp2p/status/2119770702907871743 

Partners: https://leak-detect-tooling.lovable.app/#partners 
Giveth Update: https://leak-detect-tooling.lovable.app/#giveth 
Devcon Update: https://leak-detect-tooling.lovable.app/devcon 
 
Prior ecosystem validation: LeakDetectAI was selected for the Ethereum Security Quadratic Funding round, with support from Giveth and TheDAO Security Fund. The selection and community discussion are publicly documented at https://x.com/manusheel/status/2054083699298472238 and https://github.com/SEC4AI-AI4SEC/deep-learning-sca/discussions/3 

The grant is priced below a from-scratch build because it reuses existing research, code, experimental methods, and testing infrastructure rather than funding the development of foundational side-channel analysis and AutoML capabilities again. The requested work is the focused next step: adapting and validating these capabilities against Ethereum wallet and agent threat models, building reproducible Ethereum-specific benchmarks, and working with ecosystem projects to turn findings into verified fixes and regression tests. The existing repositories provide a starting point; the Ethereum-specific integrations, validation, and adoption outcomes remain the work to be delivered by this grant.

initiative.summary: LeakDetectAI is an AI-powered security initiative that detects and helps eliminate side-channel vulnerabilities that can expose private keys, signing secrets, cryptographic operations, and sensitive transaction data across Ethereum wallets, protocols, and autonomous AI agents. The project will deploy LeakDetectAI in real-world Ethereum security workflows, working directly with ecosystem developers and maintainers to identify, reproduce, and remediate vulnerabilities. Its success will be measured through independently verifiable adoption, maintainer-accepted vulnerabilities, merged fixes, and regression tests across the Ethereum ecosystem.
initiative.title: LeakDetectAI: Detecting and Eliminating Side-Channel Vulnerabilities in Ethereum Wallets and AI Agents
